0.content:
Ayaka is Ayato's younger sister and the Kamisato Clan's public face; Inazumans call her the Shirasagi Himegimi. After their parents died the siblings agreed that he would take government affairs and she would maintain the clan's image and run its internal affairs. He is confident in her abilities but wants her to keep her innocence, to stay out of power struggles and never have to confront the darker side of life head-on. He calls shielding her from that his job as her older brother, then apologises for letting it slip. She worries about the toll his work takes and asks friends to remind him to rest.

He is proud of her, even of the outlandish things she throws into the hot pot game. He remembers that she feared thunder as a child until their mother told her it was the Shogun's voice; after that she concentrated hard at every rumble to hear what Her Excellency was saying. Through a note in his study she once asked whether she should adapt a recipe for the foreign Traveler.

In 3.3 he did not warn her what the Test of Courage would involve, reasoning that a little fright would release her tension and her friends would keep her from being too scared. In 4.3 in Fontaine he gave up his film role partly so she could bond with others without him overshadowing her (limited events).

1.content:
Thoma came to Inazuma from Mondstadt and became the Kamisato household's housekeeper; he volunteered for the work. When the clan was losing power after the parents' deaths, Ayato told him to leave if he did not want to get involved. It was partly a test of where he stood. Thoma refused to abandon "the young master and the young lady," and his Vision appeared that night. Ayato says Thoma has spared him much worry and is one of the very few people he trusts completely.

Their friendship is full of small cruelties: Ayato beats him at chess without looking at the board, has a cup of the strange creative milk he just tried delivered to Thoma (who later complains of "a glass of very peculiar-tasting milk"), and plans to give him his salt-for-sugar manjuu. Thoma says Ayato is easy to get along with "the vast majority of the time" and admires how he hands the credit to others while doing the job perfectly himself. Thoma looks after him at home because he cannot help with the politics.

2.content:
The Shuumatsuban is a secret unit that reports directly to the head of the Kamisato Clan; command passed to Ayato when his father died. He relies on it for situations he cannot be seen to touch: surveillance, intelligence, retrieving documents, finding people. Most members are orphans taken in and raised from childhood, which, as he puts it, guarantees loyalty "to the greatest extent possible." Its members' identities are closely guarded.

In his story quest one of his most trusted members, Hisashi, shadowed the Traveler's party, watched the Hiiragi clan representatives and located the Kanjou Commission's informants. After the Sakoku Decree was lifted, a Shuumatsuban agent watched the Tenryou warehouse where the Kaedehara belongings were kept (revealed in the limited 2.6 Irodori event). He hints that the Shuumatsuban is not his only resource: "If even the cunning bunny burrows thrice, then what of the cunning human?"

3.content:
The Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine has been kind to the Kamisato Clan but has never taken to Ayato personally. She calls him "the Yashiro rascal", warns that his warm smile hides scheming, and bristles at any suggestion that he is as sly as she is. Ayato is untroubled. Their work overlaps and the partnership runs smoothly, and he notes that without him she would have no one to carry out her "weird and wonderful ideas."

The clan owes her a real debt: after the Kamisato elders' failure over the Raiden Gokaden, her intervention persuaded the Shogun to show mercy. Ayato teases her indirectly, for example by leaking a slacking employee's methods to her. Together they ran the Irodori Festival (2.6), the Test of Courage (3.3) and the new Mikawa Flower Festival (5.4); he calls her ideas outlandish but often strokes of genius (limited events).

4.comment: Kamisato Ayato: The Raiden Shogun and the Kamisato oath
4.content:
His father taught him that "the Kamisato Clan stands today because of Narukami's mercy" and must follow the Shogun eternally. Ayato honours it: whatever happens in Inazuma, the Kamisato alone will never betray the Almighty Narukami. He calls himself a dutiful servant of the Shogun and uses her authority as his trump card against stubborn officials. The Shogun regards him as tricky in Tri-Commission affairs but a loyal subject, and has excused his past misdeeds.

Since the decrees ended, he speaks of the great cost that the pursuit of eternity has had for the Shogun and for Inazuma, and he sees his role as mediating while those wounds heal. In a 5.7 anecdote he comes from discussions with Her Excellency at Tenshukaku. Character Story 5 notes that "even if his heart said differently" he would bury it beneath appearances; canon does not say what that private heart holds.

5.comment: Kamisato Ayato: The Firmiana Leaf Falls (the Hiiragi affair)
5.content:
Ayato's 2.6 story quest. A rumour spread that Kujou Kamaji would marry Hiiragi Chisato, prompted by a proposal letter Chisato said she never sent. Ayato visited both, with the Traveler and Paimon in tow to spare himself small talk. He deduced that someone in the Kanjou Commission had forged the letter. With Chisato's father in prison and Chisato married into the Kujou, the Hiiragi Clan would lose its last pillar and a rival clan could take its place. The plot's leader, Matsuura, had the officer Shinnojou seized for warning Chisato.

Ayato freed Shinnojou, confronted Matsuura with the parable of the long-tongued bird and told him "You've made your move. Now, I suppose it's time I made mine." With Kamaji's help he fed the Kanjou informants a story that the marriage would marginalise the Kanjou Commission. Within two days the frightened plotters begged him to help undo it. Matsuura came to the estate to apologise, and Ayato sent Chisato back to command her clan, now recognised as indispensable.

Privately he told Chisato about his own parents' deaths, the years when he and Ayaka were treated as burdens, and that no one may ever trample over his family. To the Traveler he said everything he told Chisato was sincere, and that if you give up your stance once, you will be compromising for the rest of your life. His real aim was a Tri-Commission whose three parts restrain each other. "Stasis is not the only form of stability."

6.content:
Ayato once gave a young oni at Hanamizaka a polite pep talk about his beetle-fighting troubles, mere platitudes in Ayato's own telling. Itto took them to heart ("You can kindle the warrior spirit even in the weakest of bugs") and credits Ayato with keeping him going after his 780th defeat. Itto now calls him "my bro Ayato", says they are on the same wavelength over card games and beetle battles, and has no idea who Ayato is. Ayato finds this entirely agreeable and keeps it that way.

In the 4.4 Lantern Rite event (limited), Ayato turned up at Wangshu Inn with Itto and Kuki Shinobu. He claimed he had rushed to Liyue on a rumour of an Onikabuto contest. He called it a trip "part-business, part-leisure", praised the "Bona-Fide Beetle Battle King", and asked to take the leftovers of Itto's dish home for his family. He then remarked that Thoma would dispose of the leftover tofu as he saw fit.

7.comment: Kamisato Ayato: Kaedehara Kazuha and the Kunikuzushi secret
7.content:
The Kaedehara Clan was once a subordinate branch of the Kamisato. Ayato believes his forebears failed to save it, so he supports Kazuha today: he cannot restore the clan's fortunes, but keeping Kazuha from arrest by the Tenryou Commission is within his power. As he revealed during the limited-time 2.6 Irodori event: after the Sakoku Decree ended he noticed someone had broken into the Tenryou warehouse holding the Kaedehara belongings and taken nothing. He had Kujou Sara act as if nothing had happened and set the Shuumatsuban to watch. The intruder searched, found nothing and left Inazuma by boat. Ayato then found blank papers in a bonsai pot's hidden compartment, written in ink that appears only in water.

During the 2.6 Irodori Festival (limited), Yae Miko asked him to tease Xingqiu and an editor whom she had seen smuggling books away. Ayato turned the prank into a trail through the tale of the Five Kasen that led Kazuha to the truth: Yoshinori and a Kamisato head had confronted an eccentric named Kunikuzushi, who claimed responsibility for the failed forging of a sacred blade and defeated them all; that Kamisato head died soon afterwards of injuries from the affair. Ayato explained he had to test whether Kazuha had the will and ability to bear that truth. He also wanted Kazuha and Ayaka to have reliable friends, because "it is also very likely that you will face the same enemy together." His answer was hidden in Albedo's blank portrait, which revealed a likeness of the Balladeer when wet.

8.comment: Kamisato Ayato: The Kamisato Clan's fall and recovery
8.content:
The Kamisato are one of Inazuma's great clans and head the Yashiro Commission. Generations ago the elders' failings cost the Raiden Gokaden dearly, and only Guuji Yae's intercession saved the clan. More recently it failed to protect a swordsmith of national significance, suffered Fatui harassment and lost many people. Ayato's father worked himself to an early death trying to restore the clan, and his mother Kayo died soon after. Rivals pounced on the leaderless clan; Ayato parried smears, deceptions and frame-ups and turned them to his advantage. Today the clan's position is restored and the Yashiro Commission is unified, but Ayaka says everything of importance still rests on him.

His mother loved festival lore and used to say that the Kamisato were perhaps born to protect the gods. She told him the ritual cypress keeps its leaves even as new ones grow, and that the camellia in the courtyard stays fragrant through the bitterest winter. The household runs on notes left in his books: flowers delivered, a summons from the Guuji about land in Ritou, a report that "the Momoyo flowers have not withered."

9.content: Sayu is a Shuumatsuban ninja raised in the corps from childhood who seems to spend most of her time napping. Ayato says she looks idle but always rises to the occasion when it counts. People who do not know her habits struggle to find her; Ayato says she usually hides in the trees in the afternoon and that he has his own ways of finding her.

10.comment: Kamisato Ayato: Kujou Sara and the Tenryou Commission
10.content: Ayato calls Kujou Sara a "most formidable weapon" that old man Kujou created, and notes the flaw in the plan: Takayuki can no longer wield her. He was delighted to hear how the Traveler got Kujou Takayuki riled enough to tear his hair out. After the Sakoku Decree was lifted he asked Sara to treat a warehouse break-in as if nothing had happened, without adding guards or moving the contents (revealed in the limited 2.6 Irodori event). He works pragmatically with the Tenryou Commission's Kamaji when their interests align.

11.comment: Kamisato Ayato: Food, games and the hot pot game
11.content: Ayato eats whatever his staff plan for him, but he hunts for novelty: new snack stalls, the Milk Tea Medley in Hanamizaka, Tomoki's Dango Milk stand in Ritou, where he ordered milk with seagrass, sea ganoderma or lavender melon "for the experience." He once mixed up salt and sugar, decided savoury mizu manjuu "can work" and earmarked them for Thoma. The elderly butler Furuta begs him to leave cooking to the household. When Thoma cannot decide on dinner, the family plays the hot pot game. He suggests gifted dishes for it, and his 2025 letter jokes they have played it far too many times. He plays chess, cards and the Liyue card game "Liyue Millennial".

12.comment: Kamisato Ayato: Test of Courage (Akitsu Kimodameshi, 3.3)
12.content: During a limited-time 3.3 event the Test of Courage in Chinju Forest was Ayato's suggestion. Merchants funded it, the Kamisato provided the grounds and the Grand Narukami Shrine consulted, so it ran in three rounds. Knowing the youkai wished to hold a festival, he used the test's notoriety to draw visitors without raising expectations, then left the rest to the youkai, whose revival of the Mikawa Flower Festival followed. Yae Miko used the occasion to help the young youkai Hanyuuda Chizuru come to terms with an old parting. Ayato told no one in advance, not even Ayaka. His verdict: "Saying goodbye is also part of a festival."

13.comment: Kamisato Ayato: Fontaine and the film (Roses and Muskets, 4.3)
13.content: During a limited-time 4.3 event Ayato, Ayaka and Yoimiya arrived in Fontaine by aquabus, invited through Chiori to act in director Xavier's adaptation of "The Two Musketeers." When the investor's money fell through, Ayato suggested the courts and then fundraising before proposing they simply perform for free: for the Kamisato, ties with other nations mattered more than wealth. On set, busy negotiating cultural exchanges with the Palais Mermonia, he handed his role to Chevreuse. Director Furina rewrote the story around two sisters, played by Chevreuse and Ayaka. He admitted he also wanted Ayaka to bond with others without him. His 2024 birthday letter reports that the Inazuma-Fontaine exchanges are progressing steadily.

key: Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival
14.comment: Kamisato Ayato: Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival (5.4)
14.content: During a limited-time 5.4 event Yae Miko staged a new Mikawa Flower Festival in which human and youkai teams developed games. The Yashiro Commission arranged lodging, food, equipment and travel for every team and set the theme, announced 48 hours before opening. Ayato compiled the ritual booklets and incantation for the Guuji. He promised the Traveler he would step in if her ideas got out of hand. He was mildly exasperated that Thoma, instead of resting, signed up as a participant.

15.comment: Kamisato Ayato: Ayato's study, pens and letters
15.content: Calligraphy bored him as a boy; now he copies poems to clear his mind, and to look busy when avoiding certain people. Because servants spread word that he loves chess and calligraphy, he receives many pens as gifts, even quills from abroad. He keeps them in a wooden case and reads each gift as information about the giver. Three pens stay outside the case: a worn one on his desk for petitions; his old practice brush, once borrowed by Thoma and Ayaka, in a bottom drawer; and his mother's gift from his adulthood ceremony, sealed in silk inside an antique cabinet. His annual birthday letters invite the Traveler to the estate for spring banquets, sword-carved crystal flowers, tea from Chenyu Vale and, in 2026, a viewing of new robes and courtyard blossoms.

16.content: During a limited-time 2.6 event Ayato co-organised the Irodori Festival with Yae Miko, the first major festival after the Sakoku Decree was lifted. The Tri-Commission cooperated closely on it. The Yashiro Commission invited cultural celebrities from abroad, including the Mondstadt painter Albedo (to paint the Five Kasen) and Venti. Ayato asked the Traveler and Paimon, whom Yae had engaged as helpers, to greet the guests at Ritou harbour and guide them to their lodgings. Venti arrived passed out in a wine crate, was arrested by Kujou Sara for illegal entry, and was cleared when his invitation turned up in his hat.

17.comment: Kamisato Ayato: Kamisato Ayato: Business (5.7 anecdote)
17.content: In a Travelers' Tales anecdote (first offered during a 5.7 event, 2025-06-18), Ayato inspects fabric at Ogura Textiles & Kimonos after meeting the Shogun at Tenshukaku. Ordinary purchases are left to staff, but he chooses the fabric and colours of official ceremonial attire himself. Merchants advertise "Yashiro Commission-approved" goods after the annual procurement, and a representative he once delegated took vendors' bribes. He asks the Traveler, "Ayaka's close friend", to choose between two bolts and orders five of their choice for the estate.
